name: AutoML Object Detection Benchmark
description: Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) is a subdomain of machine learning that seeks to expand the usability of traditional machine learning methods to non-expert users by automating various tasks which normally require manual configuration. Prior benchmarking studies on AutoML systems—whose aim is to compare and evaluate their capabilities—have mostly focused on tabular or structured data. In this study, we evaluate AutoML systems on the task of object detection by curating three commonly used object detection datasets (Open Images V7, Microsoft COCO 2017, and Pascal VOC2012) in order to benchmark three different AutoML frameworks—namely, Google’s Vertex AI, NVIDIA’s TAO, and AutoGluon. We reduced the datasets to only include images with a single object instance in order to understand the effect of class imbalance, as well as dataset and object size. evaluation_method: average precision (AP) and mean average precision (mAP)
typical_sota_score: COCO (AP@[.5:.95]) roughly 40–60%; Pascal VOC (mAP@0.5) roughly 75–90%; Open Images mAP typically in the 40–60% range
notes: Non-LLM benchmark built from standard detection datasets; results depend heavily on dataset subset, class imbalance, and single-object filtering.
